Full type definitions, sizes and ownership of swap handles, snapshot handles, batch objects, bitmaps and high memory tracking entries.

findings.text: Public hibernation image operations provide a save entry that sizes the snapshot, obtains a swap writer, handles header plus plain or compressed payload, and finalizes the writer, plus a close operation that releases the resume device file unless never initialised.
Snapshot access family exposes read iteration for saving, write finalization and loaded query for restoring, and size query, with cursor driven progression across header, metadata and copy regions.
System sleep control exposes transition lock pairing, filesystem sync gate, power notifier chains, and process freeze and thaw operations for suspend preparation and resume.
Freeze and thaw serve as suspend entries that toggle global freezing state and coordinate helper gating, task freezing, OOM killer control, workqueue and thread thawing, and scheduling.

Image save and close serve as hibernation entries that accept mode flags selecting compressed or uncompressed handling, validate swap capacity in the uncompressed case, and report writer, header, payload or finalization failures.

Save iteration advances a cursor from header creation through metadata packing to copy page exposure, ending when the cursor passes metadata plus copy counts, with high memory pages staged through a shared buffer.

Restore completion is determined by cursor position relative to metadata, copy and zero counts together with copy existence and high memory drain state, with finalization draining trailing zero pages and recycling origin tracking only on full consumption.

Swap reader lifecycle constructs a linked chain of map pages from the image header, serves sequential page reads advancing within a map then discarding consumed maps, and terminates by releasing any remainder.

Hibernation input output batching tracks outstanding completions with a counter and wait queue plus latched block status and plug scope, starting empty and successful and completing when the counter returns to zero.

Uncompressed restore iterates over snapshot destinations and swap source pages using asynchronous submission with optional per page waiting, periodic progress reporting, and a final wait and finalize that requires the loaded predicate.

Compressed restore coordinates asynchronous swap reads into a page ring, per thread decompression dispatch with readiness signalling, and a separate checksum stage, progressing through read, wait, dispatch, collect and finalize phases with end of data handling.

High memory restore staging reuses the original frame through a shared buffer when that frame is both forbidden and free, otherwise records a tracking entry linking original and copy frames and selects a safe high frame when available or a safe normal page otherwise.

High memory helpers have configuration dependent forms where one build provides staging, copy completion check and data release while the alternate build reports invalid on staging, always complete on copy check, and no operation on release.
Bitmap recycling returns zone tree node and leaf storage and all linked pages to a shared safe page list without freeing the bitmap container itself.
Image header initialisation zeroes the record and populates physical page count, copy count, total image size in pages and bytes, plus system identity and version identity.

Compressed restore validates each chunk length as nonzero and within a worst case bound and each result length as nonzero, bounded and page aligned, validates overall checksum only when the header requests that mode, and treats violations as load failures.
Sleep filesystem sync ensures at most one queued sync request, waits with periodic wakeup polling, and aborts the wait when a wakeup is pending.
Power notifier delivery fans out through a shared blocking chain head in both single value and robust up down forms, translating chain results to errno in the robust case.

Compressed restore bounds worker count by online processor count minus one clamped to a configured maximum and bounds read buffering between configured minimum and maximum based on low free memory relative to image size.
Checksum helper allocates a flexible checksum object sized for worker count plus a parallel length array, and release stops the checksum thread when present and frees both allocations safely on null.
System sleep transitions serialize on a central mutex paired with a no freeze flag saved on entry and conditionally restored on exit so nested holders preserve outer state.
Thaw iterates all process threads under tasklist read protection while issuing per thread thaw, with warnings if suspend marking appears on unexpected threads or is missing on the caller.
Swap map handle observable state comprises a chain of allocated map pages, a current map pointer and index within it, and a running checksum value updated during compressed loads.

Snapshot handle observable state comprises a monotonically increasing cursor, a current data buffer pointer, and a synchronous read flag controlling whether each asynchronous swap read is waited upon immediately.
Hibernation batch observable state comprises a pending completion count, a wait queue, a latched block status, and a plug context spanning the batched submissions.

Allocation failures during map chain build, high memory staging, ring setup, thread state and checksum state cause orderly release of partial structures and return memory or fault errors, while input output errors propagate and abort the load or save.

Restore hazards include missing image pointer, null map offset, invalid compressed or uncompressed lengths, checksum mismatch, and incomplete image consumption, while suspend hazards include wakeup during filesystem sync and OOM killer disable timeout, each mapped to busy or no data failures with cleanup.
Snapshot image size is defined as the sum of copy pages and metadata pages plus one header page.

Low free memory is defined as total free pages minus free high pages, and worst case compressed size is defined as input size plus a sixteenth plus small fixed overhead, used to size read buffering and validate chunk lengths.
Image header layout carries physical page count, copy image count, total page count and byte size, together with system identity and version code.
